title: Connecting to Local Affinity MCP Server (Port 6767) & SSE Bridge
subtitle: Server-Sent Events, Upstream Tools Protocol & Health Checks

learningObjectives: Understand the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how Affinity exposes its automation tools via HTTP/SSE.
Verify the local server listener at `http://localhost:6767/sse` using status health checks.
Identify the 11 upstream MCP tools (`affinity_status`, `execute_script`, `render_spread`, `list_sdk_documentation`, etc.).
Diagnose port conflicts, firewall permissions, and application lifecycle states.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open architectural standard created by Anthropic that allows AI agents, IDE extensions, and external applications to safely interface with local desktop tools and real-time environments. Serif Affinity implements a native MCP server listening locally on port 6767 using Server-Sent Events (SSE). When an external client connects to `http://localhost:6767/sse`, Affinity establishes a full-duplex JSON-RPC communications channel, exposing capabilities like executing DOM scripts, taking real-time pixel renders of document spreads, and querying SDK documentation.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Verify Local Affinity Process is Running
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Before attempting an MCP connection, ensure Serif Affinity 3.0+ is actively running on the host machine. You can verify this via Windows Task Manager or `Get-Process Affinity` in PowerShell.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Execute the MCP Health Check Utility
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Run our verified diagnostic utility `node curriculum/assets/scripting/S01_ping_mcp.js`. The script issues a streaming HTTP GET request to `http://localhost:6767/sse` with `Accept: text/event-stream`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Inspect HTTP Response Headers and Status Code
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Verify that the server returns HTTP Status `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. This confirms that the MCP transport pipeline is established and awaiting tool invocations.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Call the affinity_status Tool
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Invoke `affinity_status`. The tool returns: `'Connected to Affinity MCP at http://localhost:6767/sse. Found 11 upstream tools.'` within ~85ms.

visualExamples.title: SSE Protocol Communications Flow
visualExamples.description: How events and tool calls flow across the local network interface.
visualExamples.visualContent:
[Web Platform / Node Client]
   │  1. HTTP GET http://localhost:6767/sse
   ├────────────────────────────────────────────────► [Affinity MCP Server]
   │  2. HTTP 200 (Content-Type: text/event-stream)
   │     event: endpoint?session_id=...
   │◄────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │  3. HTTP POST /message?session_id=... (execute_script payload)
   ├────────────────────────────────────────────────► [Evaluates in V8]
   │  4. Returns JSON-RPC Tool Result
   │◄────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

independentChallenge.title: Automated MCP Bridge Health Monitor
independentChallenge.prompt: Author a Node.js monitoring script that checks the health of `http://localhost:6767/sse` every 5 seconds. If the connection fails or times out (e.g. if the user closes Affinity), the script must output a red alert `'[ALERT] Affinity 3.0 has stopped or port 6767 is unreachable'`. When re-opened, it must display green `'[RECONNECTED]'`.
challengeCriteria: Uses native node:http module with 3000ms timeout.
Properly closes and destroys request sockets on each cycle.
Handles error events gracefully without crashing.

commonPitfalls.cause: Affinity is closed or the MCP listener is disabled in Preferences.
commonPitfalls.solution: Ensure Affinity 3.3.3 is launched and running. In Affinity, ensure MCP integration is allowed under Preferences > General / Automation.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Hanging socket connections on SSE streams
commonPitfalls.cause: Server-Sent Events keep the HTTP response socket open permanently to stream notifications.
commonPitfalls.solution: In one-shot ping scripts, always call `res.destroy()` or `req.destroy()` after reading the initial HTTP 200 headers to avoid memory leaks.

commonPitfalls.cause: The tool schema declares `topic`, but the implementation requires `filename`.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always pass `{"filename": "..."}` as documented in our Phase 1 MCP Capability Report.

knowledgeCheck.question: What HTTP Content-Type header does the Affinity MCP server return when a client connects to /sse?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Server-Sent Events require the MIME type 'text/event-stream' to maintain a persistent push channel between server and client.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary benefit of the MCP architecture for Affinity design automation compared to running standalone Node scripts?
options: It makes the computer run cooler.
It provides a standardized, secure tool-calling protocol allowing AI agents and web interfaces to inspect docs, run DOM scripts, and capture live renders with zero complex configuration.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: MCP standardizes tool schemas, execution lifecycles, and visual telemetry, enabling seamless communication between intelligent agents and creative software.

slides.title: Connecting to Local Affinity MCP Server
slides.subtitle: The Model Context Protocol Bridge at Port 6767
slides.contentMarkdown:
How do AI agents, automated pipelines, and web interfaces communicate with a running desktop creative suite?

The answer is the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**.

In this lesson, you will master the **Affinity MCP Server architecture**—learning how to connect to `http://localhost:6767/sse`, execute health pings, and harness the 11 native automation tools.

actionBox.label: The Connection
actionBox.text: Port 6767 is the high-speed gateway linking modern software to Affinity 3.0.

slides.title: How the MCP SSE Bridge Works
slides.subtitle: Server-Sent Events & JSON-RPC Telemetry
slides.contentMarkdown:
When you open Affinity 3.0, it initializes an internal HTTP server on **localhost:6767**:

1. **SSE Handshake:** The client connects to `http://localhost:6767/sse` with `Accept: text/event-stream`.
2. **Session Endpoint:** Affinity responds with an active session ID.
3. **JSON-RPC Tool Calls:** The client posts tool execution requests (e.g. `execute_script`, `render_spread`).
4. **Real-Time Delivery:** Results, logs, and base64 rendered graphics return instantly over the bridge.

visual.content: [Client / Agent] --- HTTP GET /sse ---> [Affinity Port 6767] ---> [11 Upstream Tools Ready]

slides.title: The 11 Verified MCP Upstream Tools
slides.subtitle: Your Programmatic Palette
slides.contentMarkdown:
The Affinity MCP bridge gives you access to 11 verified tools:

- **`affinity_status`:** Instant connection health ping (~85ms).
- **`execute_script`:** Executes JavaScript DOM code in the running app (~100ms).
- **`render_spread`:** Captures an active spread as a JPEG image (~180ms).
- **`render_selection`:** Captures selected node bounds as an image (~140ms).
- **`list_sdk_documentation`:** Scans all 401 SDK documentation files.
- **`read_sdk_documentation_topic`:** Reads complete API class specs.

actionBox.label: Speed Benchmark
actionBox.text: Every tool executes in under 200ms—instantaneous for real-time web previews.

slides.title: MCP Bridge Troubleshooting
slides.subtitle: Resolve Port and Connection Issues Instantly
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. ECONNREFUSED on Port 6767
- **The Issue:** Connection refused when sending requests.
- **The Fix:** Affinity is not running. Launch Affinity 3.0 and verify that automation listener is enabled.

### 2. Hanging SSE Connection Sockets
- **The Issue:** Node scripts never exit because SSE streams stay open indefinitely.
- **The Fix:** In health-check pings, always destroy the response socket (`res.destroy()`) immediately after reading the HTTP 200 header.

### 3. Topic vs Filename Parameter Schema Bug
- **Important:** `read_sdk_documentation_topic` requires parameter `filename` (not `topic`).

actionBox.text: Run npm run check:env at any time to verify local port 6767 readiness.
